history.summary: IMPORTANT: THIS IS A SIKH GURDWARA, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 806 / Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) (file 806.json, id 'harmandir-sahib-golden-temple-amritsar'), which documents the same real site. Sri Harmandir Sahib is the holiest shrine of Sikhism, built on a 67-ft square platform in the centre of the Amrit Sarovar in Amritsar. Guru Ram Das founded Amritsar and began the sarovar in 1577; Guru Arjan Dev brick-lined it and began construction in December 1588, with the foundation stone laid by the Sufi saint Mian Mir; the Adi Granth was installed in 1604 with Baba Buddha Ji as first head priest. The shrine was destroyed in a fire in the 1760s, rebuilt, and then gilded with gold and faced in marble in the early 19th century under Maharaja Ranjit Singh, giving it the name 'Golden Temple'. The complex is famous for its four entrances (openness to all), the free langar community kitchen serving tens of thousands daily, and its 24-hour operation.

name: Golden Temple (Sri Harmandir Sahib)
town_description: Amritsar is a city in northwestern Punjab, founded by the fourth Sikh Guru, Guru Ram Das, in 1577 around the sacred Amrit Sarovar. It is the spiritual and cultural centre of Sikhism, home to the Golden Temple and the Akal Takht. The city is also known for the Jallianwala Bagh memorial, its role in Partition history, and Amritsari cuisine, drawing millions of pilgrims and tourists each year.
